description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between TFLOPs (trillion floating-point operations) on the x-axis and Loss Ratio (%) on the y-axis for five different model configurations: Vanilla, SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=128), SepLLM (n=64, H), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T). The x-axis is logarithmic, ranging from 1e7 to 9e8 TFLOPs with major tick marks at 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, 1e9, 2e9, 5e9, and 9e9 (though labeled only up to 9e8), while the y-axis is linear, spanning from 94% to 99.5% Loss Ratio with tick marks every 0.5%. The “Vanilla” model (purple triangles, solid line) remains nearly flat around 99.5% across all TFLOPs. “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange squares, solid line) starts at ~98.2% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises to ~99.5% by 4e8, then fluctuates slightly around 99.3–99.5%. “SepLLM (n=128)” (blue crosses, solid line) begins at ~97.0% at 1e7 TFLOPs, climbs to ~99.5% by 5e7, and stays near 99.5% with minor dips. “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green diamonds, solid line) starts at ~97.5% at 1e7 TFLOPs, increases to ~99.5% by 5e7, and remains stable near 99.5% with small oscillations. “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red circles, solid line) begins at 94.0% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises steeply to ~98.0% at 5e7, reaches ~99.0% at 2e8, peaks at ~99.1% at 4e8, dips to ~98.5% at 5e8, then stabilizes around 98.8–99.0% through 9e8 TFLOPs. All lines show increasing or stable loss ratios with higher computational cost, with the “Vanilla” model consistently achieving the highest loss ratio.
